title: Seconds
summary: Interval names count letters. A 2nd spans two letters, and comes in a minor and a major size.

steps.title: Numbers count letters
steps.body:
Interval names use numbers. Count the letters from the first note to the second, counting both ends: C to D covers C and D, so it is a **2nd**.

**Why it matters:** The number tells you how many letters the interval covers. That is how musicians describe tunes and spell chords.

steps.title: Two sizes: minor
steps.body:
Some interval numbers come in two sizes. The smaller size is called **minor**.

**Why it matters:** Minor intervals tend to give music a darker colour. You will hear "minor" about chords and keys too.

steps.title: Two sizes: major
steps.body:
The bigger of the two sizes is called **major**.

**Why it matters:** Major intervals give music its brighter colour. "Major" and "minor" are two of the words your band uses most.

steps.title: Minor 2nd
steps.body:
A **minor 2nd** is 1 half step, like E to F or C to C♯.

**Why it matters:** It is the tightest, most tense interval. Think of the Jaws theme.

steps.title: Major 2nd
steps.body:
A **major 2nd** is 2 half steps, a whole step, like C to D.

**Why it matters:** It is the most common move in tunes. Happy Birthday steps up a major 2nd on "-py birth".

steps.title: Seconds above C
steps.body: C♯ is a minor 2nd above C, and D is a major 2nd above C.

items.prompt: Play C4, then go up a minor 2nd.
Play C4, then go up a major 2nd.
Play G4, then go up a major 2nd.
Play D4, then go up a minor 2nd.

steps.title: Small and smaller
steps.body: Play a minor 2nd, then a major 2nd, from the same key. Notice how the minor 2nd rubs and the major 2nd sounds smooth.

items.prompt: Play F4, then go up a major 2nd.
